steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Refactor 4: one seat per row** in *Normalisation*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Ben appears in two orders. An UPDATE changes his email in only one of them. Which problem is this?

steps.title: Rebuild Refactor 4: one seat per row cold
prompt: The last 1NF violation: `seats` holds lists like `'B1,B2,B3'`. Create **`order_seats(order_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id), seat TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (order_id, seat))`** and fill it with **one row per seat**.
Splitting text needs a recursive CTE: peel off the part before the first comma, then repeat on the rest.
Tables: `orders_flat(order_id, customer_name, customer_email, show_title, show_date, seats, price_each)`, plus your `customers`, `shows` and `orders`.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
